content: The Steering Group, in collaboration with the Guideline Development Group (GDG), selected and confirmed nine technical experts and stakeholders with expertise in thematic areas relevant to the recommendations in this guideline. These individuals were appointed as members of the External Review Group (ERG). After the GDG meeting and subsequent revisions to the draft guideline, the document was shared with the ERG members. Their role was to provide feedback on the accuracy, clarity of language, implementation and adaptation considerations, and the presentation of the guideline. The finalized recommendations, as determined by the GDG, were not altered based on ERG input except to improve clarity and readability. All comments from the ERG were compiled by the responsible technical officer and reviewed by the WHO Steering Group. In line with the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2014), representatives from various professional organizations and United Nations agencies were invited to attend the GDG meeting in April 2021 as observers. These observers, including representatives from the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG), the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO), the International Confederation of Midwives (ICM), and the International Council of Nurses (ICN), had no role in determining the recommendations. Representatives from all invited organizations, except ICN, attended. Additionally, implementing partner organizations such as Ipas, the International Planned Parenthood Federation (IPPF), MSI Reproductive Choices, Pathfinder, and Population Services International (PSI) were invited to review the draft guideline before its submission to the Guidelines Review Committee (GRC). All consultants and collaborators involved in the guideline development process were required to declare any competing interests (academic, financial, or other) in writing at the time of their invitation. This was done through the electronic submission of a signed WHO Declaration of Interests (DOI) form and a copy of their curriculum vitae. Internet searches were also conducted to identify any undisclosed potential conflicts of interest. Participants were informed that failure to complete and sign a DOI form would preclude their participation in meetings. The responsible technical officer assessed the DOI forms and CVs in consultation with the Director of the Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) Department and the WHO Steering Group to determine the existence and severity of any conflicts of interest and to develop a management plan. One ERG member was found to have a conflict of interest during the guideline development process and was excluded from further meetings. No other conflicts of interest were identified. The eligibility of ERG, GDG, and ERRG members was confirmed after this process, and all participants were instructed to notify the responsible technical officer of any changes in relevant interests during their involvement. At the start of each meeting, participants were given the opportunity to verbally confirm, amend, or append their declared interests. They could also do so in writing before submitting comments on draft versions of the guideline. All members of the ERG, GDG, ERRG, and Evidence Synthesis Teams (ESTs), as well as guideline methodologists, were required to sign confidentiality agreements related to the guideline development process and outcomes. The responsible technical officer securely stored all DOI forms and CVs to maintain confidentiality. The scope of the guidance was defined through an online survey conducted in September 2018 to identify areas requiring updates or new additions to the WHO guidance on safe abortion. The survey also sought suggestions for making the guidelines more user-friendly and received 122 responses. Scoping meetings for the three domains of the guideline—Clinical Services, Service Delivery, and Law and Policy—were held between November 2018 and June 2019. These meetings aimed to identify key topic areas and formulate key questions in the PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes) format. The PICO questions were further refined through email exchanges between the WHO Steering Group and ERRG members. Additional technical meetings addressed issues such as abortion care in humanitarian settings, values and preferences related to abortion care, and youth concerns. The evidence review process involved systematic reviews of randomized controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomized trials, cohort studies, and other relevant research. The GRADE approach was used to assess the quality of evidence, which was categorized as high, moderate, low, or very low. Evidence summaries, including GRADE tables and Evidence-to-Decision (EtD) frameworks, were prepared for each PICO question. The WHO-INTEGRATE framework was used to evaluate interventions across six criteria: health benefits and harms, human rights and sociocultural acceptability, health equity, societal implications, financial considerations, and feasibility. This framework was particularly suited for complex interventions and allowed for informed decision-making across all domains. The GDG meeting in April 2021 reviewed and finalized the draft recommendations. Decisions were made by consensus whenever possible, with voting used in one instance where consensus could not be reached. Following the meeting, revisions were made to reflect the GDG’s deliberations and feedback. The revised draft was shared with GDG members, ERG members, meeting observers, and implementing partner organizations for further comments. The Steering Group reviewed all feedback and incorporated it into the final guideline document, which was approved by the GRC in August 2021 after requested revisions were completed.
